cards.text: Friend, the Philistine commanders didn't want David with them in their battle against Israel, so Achish, king of Gath, sent David and his men back home. On the third day they make it to Ziklag, and you know that feeling when all you want is your own chair. But while they were gone, the Amalekites raided the Negev and attacked Ziklag.

cards.question: While David and his men were away, the Amalekites attacked Ziklag and ___ it down.
The Amalekites killed everyone they found in Ziklag.

cards.text: David's men walk into town and see it all. The town is burned down, and their wives and sons and daughters have been taken captive.

cards.question: Homes burned and families gone. What do David and his men do?

answers.text: Weep until they have no strength left
Sit in silence for seven days
Chase the raiders that same hour

cards.question: Two of the captives are David's own wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and ___ the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

cards.text: Now David is greatly distressed. The soul of every man is grieving for his sons and daughters, and that grief is looking for somewhere to land.

cards.question: In all that grief, what do the people in David's camp start talking about?
His town is gone, his family is gone and his own men are turning on him. Where does David find strength?

cards.text: Then David says to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, "Bring me the ephod." So Abiathar brings it to him.

cards.question: Once Abiathar brings the ephod, David inquires of the LORD.
David asks the LORD, "Should I pursue these raiders? Will I overtake them?" What does the LORD tell him?

answers.text: Pursue and you will rescue the captives
Stay and rebuild your town first
Wait here and they will come back

cards.text: So David and his six hundred men take off and reach the Brook of Besor. They already walked three days to get home and now it's a chase, so friend, my legs hurt just TELLING this.

cards.question: At the Brook of Besor, ___ of David's six hundred men are too exhausted to cross.
David waits at the Brook of Besor until his exhausted men are ready to cross.

cards.text: Out in a field, David's men find an Egyptian and bring him to David. The man is in rough shape.

cards.question: David's men tie up the Egyptian they found in the field as a spy.

cards.text: They give him water, a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he eats and is revived. I know that look, friend, because that's me when somebody yells FRESH BATCH across the bakery.

cards.question: Why was the Egyptian so weak when David's men found him?

answers.text: No food or water for three days
Wounded in the raid on Ziklag
Lost in the desert for weeks

cards.text: Once the Egyptian can sit up, David asks him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?"

cards.question: The Egyptian tells David he's a slave, and his master is ___.
The Egyptian's master left him behind three days ago because he tried to escape.

cards.text: He tells David they raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah and the Negev of Caleb, and "we burned down Ziklag." WE, friend, and he's telling that to the man who LIVES in Ziklag.
I think David's got one thing on his mind now. He asks him, "Will you lead me to these raiders?"

cards.question: Before he'll lead David to the raiders, what does the Egyptian ask David to swear by God?

answers.text: Not to kill him or hand him over
To give him a share of the plunder
To send him safely home to Egypt

cards.text: So he leads David down, and there they are. The Amalekites, spread out over all the land.

cards.question: David finds the Amalekites spread out over all the land. What are they doing?

cards.text: David strikes them down from twilight until the evening of the next day. Friend, that's not a battle, that's a DOUBLE SHIFT.

cards.question: Not a single Amalekite gets away from David.
Four hundred young men escape on camels, and that's it. Of everything the Amalekites took, how much does David bring back?

cards.text: Nothing's missing, including his two wives, and his men drive the flocks and herds out ahead, calling out, "This is David's plunder!" Friend, that's not a march home, that's a PARADE.
Back at the Brook of Besor, the two hundred men who were too exhausted to follow come out to meet them, and David greets them. Sounds nice, but hold that thought.

cards.question: The wicked and worthless men who went into battle with David have a plan for the two hundred who stayed behind. What is it?

answers.text: Give them only their wives and children
Make them carry all the plunder home
Send them back to the Philistine army

cards.question: David calls those men "My brothers" and tells them they must not do this. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD gave it and protected them
The two hundred are his own family
Saul would punish them for it

cards.question: So David rules on the plunder: the share of the one who went to battle will ___ the share of the one who stayed with the supplies.
David's rule about sharing alike becomes a statute and ordinance for Israel.

cards.text: When David gets back to Ziklag, he doesn't stack all that plunder in a corner and admire it. He starts sending some of it out.

cards.question: David sends some of the plunder as "a gift for you from the plunder of the LORD's enemies." He sends it to his friends, the ___ of Judah.

cards.text: Then the gifts go out all over, to Bethel, Jattir, Hormah, Hebron and every place where David and his men had roamed. That's a LOT of boxes to pack, friend, and I say that as a professional. Keep your apron on, because David's story isn't over yet.

findings.problem: The card tells events from 1 Samuel 29: the Philistine commanders refusing David and Achish sending him home. It cites only 1 Samuel 30:1, so those facts have no reference.

findings.problem: The question says "his own men are turning on him," which rules out the wrong answer "In his loyal mighty men." That leaves only two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
